reference_solution: Keep an event-ID dictionary containing the immutable accepted payload and a list of accepted events. Validate values, then check the ID dictionary first so exact replays remain idempotent. For a new ID, reject timestamps below the current watermark, accept the event, and advance the maximum timestamp. Sum half-open windows over accepted records.
explanation: Deduplication must precede lateness evaluation because a previously accepted retry is not a new late event. The watermark is based on the greatest event time observed, not wall time. Half-open intervals compose without double-counting boundaries.

alternatives.name: Sorted timestamp index
alternatives.solution: Insert accepted events into a bisectable timestamp index with prefix sums.

trade_off_analysis: The reference gives simple O(n) queries and unbounded retention.
A production dedupe horizon can save memory but changes replay guarantees.
Distributed exactly-once effects require durable identity state, not only an in-process dictionary.

complexity.expected_time: record is O(1) average and sum_between is O(n).
complexity.explanation: The explicit list favors semantic clarity; an indexed design can optimize query load.

testing_and_debugging: Test exact and conflicting duplicates before and after watermark advancement.
Test exact watermark, just-below watermark, and exclusive window end.
production_follow_ups: Partition watermark and identity state by key.
Persist dedupe entries with a retention contract and audit late-event loss.
critical_omissions: Duplicate check performed after lateness rejection.
strong_response_example: I will validate, check the event ID first, and return False for an exact replay regardless of the current watermark. Only a new ID is compared with max_event_time minus allowed_lateness. Queries use [start, end) so adjacent windows do not overlap.

boundary_error: Use an event exactly at the watermark
